instruction: Extract only the neural network model definitions (BigramLanguageModel class with all its methods) from Karpathy's GPT colab code cells and save to "gpt_model.py" in Home directory. Include the complete class implementation.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the BigramLanguageModel class from Karpathy's GPT colab. The class should contain at least the __init__, forward, and generate methods. Evaluator verifies: (1) class BigramLanguageModel exists, (2) contains at least 2 of the 3 required methods. Partial credit: 0.4 for class existence, 0.2 per method found.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete coverage: Instruction requires 'all its methods' and 'complete class implementation', but evaluator only checks for 3 specific methods (__init__, forward, generate). BigramLanguageModel may have additional methods that won't be verified.
Lenient threshold: min_methods=2 allows passing with only 2 out of 3 methods, which doesn't align with 'complete class implementation' requirement.
No completeness verification: Evaluator only checks method name existence via AST, not whether methods have actual implementations vs empty stubs.
Missing exclusivity check: Instruction says extract 'only' model definitions, but evaluator doesn't verify that non-model code (training loops, data loading, etc.) was excluded.
Getter and metric logic are correct: get_vm_file properly retrieves the file, and AST parsing is appropriate for analyzing Python class structure.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change min_methods from 2 to 3 to require all three specified methods for full credit, better aligning with 'complete class implementation' requirement.
Consider verifying method implementations are non-trivial (e.g., check that method body has more than just 'pass' or 'return None').
Add check that the file contains only the BigramLanguageModel class definition and no training/data loading code.
If possible, enumerate all actual methods in Karpathy's BigramLanguageModel and verify all are present, not just the 3 core ones.
Adjust partial credit logic: require all 3 methods for scores above 0.8, since instruction emphasizes completeness.
